Audio Priority Bar 2.2.0 makes paired USB headset selection explicit and configurable, simplifies device hiding, tightens menu bar icon spacing, and refreshes Jabra status immediately. Upgrading from 2.1.0 preserves existing priorities, categories, visibility, and the previous microphone pairing preference.

## Headset selection

- **Select headset input and output together** is enabled by default. Selecting either half of a physical USB headset in the panel selects the other half too.
- A paired row offers **Mic only** or **Output only** while paired selection is enabled, and **Use both** while it is disabled. The override appears only when it would change the current selection.
- The setting replaces the previous microphone pairing preference and keeps its existing value during the upgrade.

## Device management

- **Hide Device** now has one meaning. It hides a microphone from Microphones or an output from both Speakers and Headphones, regardless of its current category.
- **Show hidden and disconnected devices** reveals every hidden or remembered device for management.
- Moving an output between Speakers and Headphones preserves whether it is hidden, and the active microphone remains visible even when hidden.
- **Never Auto-Select** remains independent from visibility, so a device can stay visible without being chosen automatically.

## Menu bar and status

- The menu bar item no longer reserves excess horizontal space. Its speaker icon now matches the narrower two-wave symbol used by macOS.
- A Jabra Link status change redraws its row immediately, so **Headset off** no longer waits for hover or another panel update.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is ad-hoc signed, not signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
